parsed.explanation: Combined regime: strong state-level protections for facilities, discrimination, hate crime and shield-law care, but national entry screening, national-facility rules and national custody remain controlling at the border and in federal custody. Document/marker discrepancy can trigger refusal and, if wilful misrepresentation is suspected, consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; confiscations and strandings are documented. If admitted, local bathroom, school, anti-discrimination and care protections materially improve the visit, yet they do not cancel federal exposures. Severity after outing at entry/custody is major, probability of outing at document checks is high, so below the 0.65-0.75 tier but above purely national-average risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary sex definition, X-marker passports stopped Feb 2025, Supreme Court allowed restriction Nov 2025; visa cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt and consideration of permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation; passports confiscated/blocked and travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration. State offers X on licences/IDs and birth-certificate self-attestation, but source states state law does not govern passports, visas or entry screening.
entry_documents.interaction: State protections do not alter port-of-entry encounter; discrepancy can move applicant into refusal/investigation and possible fraud finding, with lawsuits pending and not restoring entry in real time.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model including short haircuts, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No protective custody-placement protocol for visitors is sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy can lead to detention; national custody harms and birth-sex/facility definitions then apply, outside state protective law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Jan 2025 order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity nationally; federal buildings in the state remain under national rule.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State: single-occupancy public restrooms gender-neutral since 2020; largest city allows bathroom access by self-determined identity, all-gender school bathrooms since Dec 2021; state in no-ban/most-protective tier.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local public facilities are comparatively protective, federal facilities are not; statewide multi-occupancy bill passed chambers but signing/veto unresolved, so statewide rule is uncertain.

care_services.exposure: National orders target gender-affirming care for minors, funding restrictions, hospital subpoenas for minor patient records, and Oct 2025 proposed insurance bar for under-18 care.
care_services.protection: 2023 shield law protects patients and providers from civil/criminal charges where care lawful in state was banned in home jurisdiction, including travellers from outside; conversion therapy on minors banned since 2016.
care_services.interaction: Shield protects local care access, including for travelling minors, but dossier does not source whether it withstands federal subpoenas or national enforcement.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy May 2026 says it will prioritize rapid identification/neutralization of groups described as radically pro-transgender; Dec 2025 reward memo uses radical gender ideology twice, though not as reward criterion; teacher-prosecution directive for social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime penalties extended to gender identity in 2016, gay/trans panic defence repealed 2018, discrimination banned since 2006, courts dismissed challenge to conversion-therapy ban in 2017.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat framing raises outing/investigation risk, while state law provides local criminal and civil recourse; several national orders are blocked/enjoined or litigated.

minors_guardians.exposure: Nationally, youth care banned in 27 states, LGBTQ youth crisis services shut down July 2025, teachers may face investigation/prosecution for facilitating social transition, schools threatened over trans content.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield law covers travelling patients, bullying based on gender identity/expression prohibited with privacy protections, 2019 task force on names/pronouns/dress codes, conversion therapy on minors banned.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor is better protected locally than nationally, but national school/funding and home-jurisdiction rules can still interact; shield addresses home-jurisdiction charges for lawful local care.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2025 national poll: 66% support assigned-sex on licences/passports, 69% support assigned-sex sports rules; national hostility and allied travel advisories documented. State hate-crime prosecution data not sourced.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime enhanced penalties since 1991 for sexual orientation and since 2016 for gender identity; public-accommodations discrimination banned; local police response data not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local law is protective on paper, but absence of enforcement/outcome data and national climate mean street-level recourse is documented as law, not as proven practice.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport-marker suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs is pending after Supreme Court allowed restriction; multiple executive orders challenged, several blocked/enjoined, outcomes unresolved at travel time.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on passport rules; state courts dismissed anti-conversion-ban challenge; discrimination and hate-crime statutes provide local claims.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow and uncertain at the border where refusal occurs, stronger for in-state discrimination/care/facilities after admission.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: extended secondary screening for document divergence, discretionary refusal and slow/rarely revised remedies. This case is near that anchor for entry, but local facilities/care protections are stronger than in the anchor, lifting it slightly above 0.55.

Higher safety than this case: clinic refusal was overturned within hours by an ombudsperson with prescription arranged. Here border refusal/fraud-ineligibility risk has only pending litigation and Supreme Court permission for the restriction, so remedies do not work quickly at entry.

Higher safety: entry on matching markers, brief detention ending in release, tribunal and compensation. Here discrepancy can support refusal and permanent ineligibility consideration, and national custody abuse is documented, placing it materially below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is sequential: national document/entry rules create the main outing and refusal risk, potentially escalating to detention with documented national custody harms; state law does not preempt those federal stages. Once admitted, the state shifts risk down through no local bathroom ban, gender-neutral single-occupancy facilities, city self-ID access, anti-discrimination and hate-crime law, and a shield law for travelling patients/minors. That protective local layer is real and operative, but federal entry, federal facilities and custody exposures govern the journey's sharpest moments, keeping the combined regime at elevated rather than reduced risk.
